from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine Leo the Lion walking across a field.",
            "A position graph shows his location over time.",
            "A velocity graph tracks his speed every second."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Language of Motion", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        LION_COLOR = "#E3CF57"
        POS_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        VEL_COLOR = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(LION_COLOR))
        
        # Lion Icon
        lion_body = Circle(radius=0.3, color=LION_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        lion_face = Triangle(color=LION_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).rotate(-PI/2).move_to(lion_body.get_right())
        lion = VGroup(lion_body, lion_face)
        self.place_at_grid(lion, 'D1', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Ground line
        ground = Line(self.grid['D1'] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid['D6'] + RIGHT*0.5, color=GREY_C)
        self.add(ground)
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_lion(obj):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            start_pos = self.grid['D1']
            end_pos = self.grid['D6']
            obj.move_to(start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (t/4))
            
        lion.add_updater(update_lion)
        self.add(lion)
        
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(POS_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Position Axes - use label_constructor=Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        pos_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 18}
        ).add_coordinates(label_constructor=Text)
        
        pos_label = Text("Position (m)", font_size=16, color=POS_COLOR)
        pos_axes_group = VGroup(pos_axes, pos_label)
        pos_label.next_to(pos_axes, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(pos_axes_group, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(pos_axes), Write(pos_label))
        
        # Position Line (Linear growth: y = x)
        pos_line = Line(pos_axes.c2p(0, 0), pos_axes.c2p(0, 0), color=POS_COLOR)
        def update_pos_line(line):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            line.set_points_as_corners([pos_axes.c2p(0, 0), pos_axes.c2p(t, t)])
            
        pos_line.add_updater(update_pos_line)
        self.add(pos_line)
        
        # Reset lion and time for visualization
        lion.remove_updater(update_lion)
        time_tracker.set_value(0)
        lion.add_updater(update_lion)
        
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(VEL_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Velocity Axes - use label_constructor=Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        vel_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 18}
        ).add_coordinates(label_constructor=Text)
        
        vel_label = Text("Velocity (m/s)", font_size=16, color=VEL_COLOR)
        vel_axes_group = VGroup(vel_axes, vel_label)
        vel_label.next_to(vel_axes, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(vel_axes_group, 'E1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(vel_axes), Write(vel_label))
        
        # Velocity Line (Constant growth: y = 1)
        vel_line = Line(vel_axes.c2p(0, 1), vel_axes.c2p(0, 1), color=VEL_COLOR)
        def update_vel_line(line):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            line.set_points_as_corners([vel_axes.c2p(0, 1), vel_axes.c2p(t, 1)])
            
        vel_line.add_updater(update_vel_line)
        self.add(vel_line)
        
        # Reset everything for final sweep
        lion.remove_updater(update_lion)
        time_tracker.set_value(0)
        lion.add_updater(update_lion)
        
        # Position and velocity lines update via time_tracker and updaters
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Derivative: Zooming into the Slope"
        lines = [
            "The derivative measures the local rate of change.",
            "Zooming in reveals a straight tangent line.",
            "The slope of this line is instantaneous speed.",
            "The derivative of position gives us velocity."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Helper colors
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        DOT_COLOR = "#FF0000"    # Red
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#00BFFF" # Deep Sky Blue
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FF00" # Green

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Curved function f(x) = sin(x) + 2
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CURVE_COLOR)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 2, x_range=[0, 5], color=CURVE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Red dot and magnifying circle focus
        self.lecture[1].set_color(DOT_COLOR)
        
        # ValueTracker for the dot's x position
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        
        dot = Dot(color=DOT_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), np.sin(x_tracker.get_value()) + 2)))
        
        # Magnifying circle
        magnifier = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        magnifier.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(dot.get_center()))
        
        # Focus effect: We'll show a zoomed version of the curve inside a circle 
        # For simplicity and performance, we'll simulate the "zoom" by scaling a segment of the curve
        def get_zoomed_segment():
            curr_x = x_tracker.get_value()
            # Plot a very small segment around curr_x and scale it
            zoom_range = [curr_x - 0.2, curr_x + 0.2]
            seg = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 2, x_range=zoom_range, color=CURVE_COLOR)
            # Create a localized zoom display
            zoom_box = Circle(radius=0.8).move_to(self.grid["B5"]) # Positioned to the side
            seg.scale(5, about_point=axes.c2p(curr_x, np.sin(curr_x) + 2))
            seg.move_to(zoom_box.get_center())
            # Clip the segment to the zoom box
            clipped_seg = Intersection(seg, zoom_box, color=CURVE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0)
            return VGroup(zoom_box, seg)

        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(magnifier))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Tangent line and label
        self.lecture[2].set_color(TANGENT_COLOR)
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            x = x_tracker.get_value()
            slope = np.cos(x)
            # Line length
            l = 1.5
            p1 = axes.c2p(x - l/2, (np.sin(x) + 2) - (l/2)*slope)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x + l/2, (np.sin(x) + 2) + (l/2)*slope)
            return Line(p1, p2, color=TANGENT_COLOR)

        tangent_line = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        
        slope_label = Text("Slope = Derivative", font_size=16, color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(tangent_line), Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Dynamic movement
        self.lecture[3].set_color(VELOCITY_COLOR)
        
        # Add a velocity vector visual (optional but helps "derivative of position is velocity")
        # We will just animate the movement across the curve
        
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Return to center
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the lecture lines for layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "The integral represents the total accumulation of progress.",
            "It calculates the area under a velocity curve.",
            "We sum infinite tiny slices of speed together.",
            "This area reveals the total distance covered."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout("The Integral: Shading the Accumulation", lecture_lines)

        # Color palette
        COLOR_CURVE = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        COLOR_BARS = "#FFD700"   # Yellow
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFA500"   # Orange

        # Setup Axes and Graph elements
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)

        # Velocity function: v(t) = 0.5*sin(1.5t) + 2
        def v_func(t):
            return 0.5 * np.sin(1.5 * t) + 2.0

        curve = axes.plot(v_func, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        curve_label = Text("v(t)", color=COLOR_CURVE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "B6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: A wavy velocity curve v(t) is drawn in cyan (#00FFFF) on the screen.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE))
        self.play(
            Write(axes),
            Create(curve),
            Write(curve_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: Five thick vertical bars (#FFD700) fill the space between the curve and the x-axis.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_BARS))
        rects_5 = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0.5, 4.5], 
            dx=0.8, 
            color=COLOR_BARS, 
            fill_opacity=0.5, 
            stroke_width=2
        )
        self.play(Create(rects_5), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: The bars multiply into 50 thin slices, fitting the curve's shape precisely.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_BARS))
        rects_50 = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0.5, 4.5], 
            dx=0.08, 
            color=COLOR_BARS, 
            fill_opacity=0.5, 
            stroke_width=0.1
        )
        self.play(Transform(rects_5, rects_50), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Description: The slices blend into a semi-transparent orange (#FFA500) shaded area 
        # and the label 'Accumulated Distance (Integral)' appears.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_AREA))
        
        integral_area = axes.get_area(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0.5, 4.5], 
            color=COLOR_AREA, 
            opacity=0.4
        )
        
        integral_label = Text("Accumulated Distance (Integral)", font_size=24, color=COLOR_AREA)
        self.place_at_grid(integral_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(rects_5, integral_area),
            Write(integral_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "The Grand Connection: Two Sides of the Same Coin"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Integration and differentiation are actually inverse operations.",
            "Derivatives break paths down into instantaneous speeds.",
            "Integrals build those speeds back into total paths.",
            "They are two sides of the same mathematical coin."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        pink_color = "#FF69B4"
        green_color = "#32CD32"
        formula_color = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create boxes
        diff_box = Rectangle(width=1.8, height=1.2, color=pink_color, fill_opacity=0.2)
        diff_label = Text("Differentiate", font_size=18, color=pink_color)
        diff_group = VGroup(diff_box, diff_label)
        self.place_at_grid(diff_group, "C2")
        
        int_box = Rectangle(width=1.8, height=1.2, color=green_color, fill_opacity=0.2)
        int_label = Text("Integrate", font_size=18, color=green_color)
        int_group = VGroup(int_box, int_label)
        self.place_at_grid(int_group, "C5")

        self.play(Create(diff_group), Create(int_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(pink_color)

        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' command dependency
        fx = Text("f(x)", color=formula_color, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(fx, "C1")
        
        # Emerging derivative f'(x)
        dfx = Text("f'(x)", color=formula_color, font_size=32)
        mid_point = (self.grid["C3"] + self.grid["C4"]) / 2
        dfx.move_to(mid_point)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(fx))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move f(x) into pink box and emerge as f'(x)
        self.play(fx.animate.move_to(diff_group.get_center()), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(fx, shift=RIGHT), FadeIn(dfx, shift=RIGHT))
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(green_color)

        # Original result f(x) + C
        fx_c = Text("f(x) + C", color=formula_color, font_size=32)
        fx_c.move_to(self.grid["C6"])
        
        # Move f'(x) into green box and emerge as f(x) + C
        self.play(dfx.animate.move_to(int_group.get_center()), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(dfx, shift=RIGHT), FadeIn(fx_c, shift=RIGHT))
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show connection: Curved arrow from end back to start
        arrow = CurvedArrow(
            start_point=self.grid["B6"] + UP*0.5, 
            end_point=self.grid["B1"] + UP*0.5, 
            angle=-TAU/4, 
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Visualizing the Link: The Area Function", 
            [
                "The rate of area growth equals the curve's height.", 
                "This link bridges the gap between slope and area.", 
                "The derivative of the integral returns the original function."
            ]
        )

        # Define functions
        def f_func(t):
            return 0.3 * t + 0.4
        
        def a_func(x):
            return 0.15 * (x**2) + 0.4 * x

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#32CD32"  # Lime green
        COLOR_AREA = "#87CEEB" # Light blue
        COLOR_A = "#FF4500"  # Orange-red
        COLOR_FORMULA = "#FFFFFF"

        # Axes for f(t) - Bottom
        axes_bottom = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 16}
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        
        label_f = Text("f(t)", color=COLOR_F, font_size=20)
        self.place_in_area(axes_bottom, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        label_f.move_to(axes_bottom.c2p(3.8, 1.8))

        # Axes for A(x) - Top
        axes_top = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 16}
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        
        label_A = Text("A(x)", color=COLOR_A, font_size=20)
        self.place_in_area(axes_top, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        label_A.move_to(axes_top.c2p(3.8, 3.5))

        # Plot Graphs
        f_graph = axes_bottom.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_F)
        A_graph = axes_top.plot(a_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_A)

        # Value Tracker for dynamic x
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Area under f(t)
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes_bottom.get_area(
            f_graph, 
            x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()], 
            color=COLOR_AREA, 
            opacity=0.5
        ))

        # Dot and Vertical line on A(x)
        dot_A = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes_top.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), a_func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_A
        ))
        
        v_line_A = always_redraw(lambda: axes_top.get_vertical_line(
            dot_A.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2
        ))

        # Dot and Vertical line on f(t)
        dot_f = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes_bottom.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), f_func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_F
        ))

        v_line_f = always_redraw(lambda: axes_bottom.get_vertical_line(
            dot_f.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2
        ))

        # Grouping and Animation
        self.add(axes_bottom, axes_top, label_f, label_A)
        self.play(Create(f_graph), Create(A_graph))
        self.add(area, dot_A, v_line_A, dot_f, v_line_f)

        # Animate the sweep
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the stage
        title = "Conclusion: The Universal Cycle"
        lines = [
            "Derivatives find the slope; integrals find the area.",
            "Together, they power physics, engineering, and economics.",
            "They form a perfect cycle of mathematical change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # Speedometer Icon (#00FFFF)
        speedometer = VGroup()
        speed_arc = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color="#00FFFF")
        speed_ticks = VGroup(*[
            Line(0.6 * UP, 0.7 * UP, color="#00FFFF").rotate(a, about_point=ORIGIN)
            for a in np.linspace(0, PI, 5)
        ])
        speed_needle = Line(ORIGIN, 0.6 * UP, color="#00FFFF").rotate(-PI/4, about_point=ORIGIN)
        speedometer.add(speed_arc, speed_ticks, speed_needle)
        self.place_in_area(speedometer, "B1", "C2", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Odometer Icon (#FFD700)
        odometer = VGroup()
        odo_rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.6, color="#FFD700")
        odo_text = Text("8429.3", font_size=18, color="#FFD700")
        odometer.add(odo_rect, odo_text)
        self.place_in_area(odometer, "B5", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(speedometer), Create(odometer))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700")
        )

        # Labels for the cycle
        deriv_label = Text("Derivative", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        integ_label = Text("Integral", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_label, "D2", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(integ_label, "D5", scale_factor=0.9)

        # Circular loop arrows (#FFFFFF)
        # Top arrow: Speedometer to Odometer
        arrow_top = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid["B2"] + 0.4 * UP + 0.4 * RIGHT,
            self.grid["B5"] + 0.4 * UP + 0.4 * LEFT,
            angle=-TAU/4,
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Bottom arrow: Odometer to Speedometer
        arrow_bottom = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid["C5"] + 0.4 * DOWN + 0.4 * LEFT,
            self.grid["C2"] + 0.4 * DOWN + 0.4 * RIGHT,
            angle=-TAU/4,
            color=WHITE
        )

        self.play(
            Write(deriv_label),
            Write(integ_label),
            Create(arrow_top),
            Create(arrow_bottom)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Pulsing effect: Labels and arrows pulse in sync
        pulse_group = VGroup(deriv_label, integ_label, arrow_top, arrow_bottom)
        
        # Two pulses to represent the cycle
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                pulse_group.animate.scale(1.15),
                rate_func=there_and_back,
                run_time=0.8
            )
            self.wait(0.1)

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Dance of Change and Accumulation: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Motion
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite concepts of 'Position' and 'Velocity'. Establish the foundational understanding that a graph can represent physical movement. Briefly define a function f(x) as a path on a coordinate plane.
sections.example: Visualize 'Leo the Lion' walking across a field. A position-time graph shows where he is, while a velocity-time graph shows how fast he is moving at any given second.

sections.title: The Derivative: Zooming into the Slope
sections.content: Explain the derivative as the 'Rate of Change.' Use the concept of zooming in on a curve until it looks like a straight line. Key concept: The derivative of the position function gives us the velocity function.
sections.example: Animation: Zoom in on Leo's position curve. As we zoom, the curve flattens into a tangent line. The slope of this line is Leo's 'Instantaneous Speed' (the derivative).

sections.title: The Integral: Shading the Accumulation
sections.content: Introduce the definite integral as the 'Total Accumulation' or the 'Area Under the Curve.' If we know the speed at every moment, how do we find the total distance traveled? Key concept: Summing up infinite tiny slices of progress.
sections.example: Graphic: Look at Leo's velocity-time graph. Divide the area under the curve into thin rectangles. Shading these rectangles represents the total distance Leo has covered from start to finish.

sections.title: The Grand Connection: Two Sides of the Same Coin
sections.content: Introduce the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Explain that integration and differentiation are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. If you take the derivative of an integral, you get the original function back.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Calculus Machine' device. Feed a Position Function into the 'Derivative Slot' to get Velocity. Feed that Velocity into the 'Integral Slot' to reconstruct the original Position Function (plus a constant C).

sections.title: Visualizing the Link: The Area Function
sections.content: Show how the rate at which the area under a curve grows is exactly equal to the height of the curve at that point. This is the visual proof of why the derivative of the area (integral) is the function itself.
sections.example: Animation: A vertical line (the 'scanner') moves across a curve from left to right, shading the area. A secondary graph tracks the 'Speed of Shading.' This second graph perfectly matches the height of the original curve.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Universal Cycle
sections.content: Summarize the flow: Derivative = Slope/Rate; Integral = Area/Total. Emphasize that knowing one allows us to unlock the other, which is essential for physics, engineering, and economics.
sections.example: A final summary graphic showing a circular arrow between a 'Speedometer' (Derivative) and an 'Odometer' (Integral), illustrating the perfect balance between the two.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Motion
lecture_lines: Imagine Leo the Lion walking across a field.
A position graph shows his location over time.
A velocity graph tracks his constant speed.
animations: A small lion icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lion.svg] (#E3CF57) moves from left to right at a constant speed across the screen.
A position-time graph appears above the lion, with a green line (#00FF00) tracing his progress linearly.
A velocity-time graph appears below the lion, showing a constant horizontal cyan line (#00FFFF) representing his steady speed.

storyboard.title: The Derivative: Zooming into the Slope
lecture_lines: A curve represents varying movement over time.
Let's focus on one specific point.
Zooming in reveals a straight line segment.
This tangent's slope is the derivative.
The derivative changes as the slope fluctuates.
animations: A curved function f(x) = sin(x) + 2 is drawn in yellow (#FFFF00) on a coordinate plane.
A red dot (#FF0000) appears on the curve, and a magnifying circle focus on it.
Inside the circle, the curve is zoomed in until it appears as a straight line segment.
A tangent line (#00BFFF) is drawn through the dot, with a label 'Slope = Derivative'.
The dot moves along the curve, and the tangent line rotates to match the changing slope dynamically.

storyboard.title: The Integral: Shading the Accumulation
lecture_lines: Velocity graphs show how speed changes.
We approximate the area using simple blocks.
Thinner slices provide a more accurate total.
The integral represents this total shaded area.
Area under velocity gives the total distance.
animations: A wavy velocity curve v(t) is drawn in cyan (#00FFFF) on the screen.
Five thick vertical bars (#FFD700) fill the space between the curve and the x-axis to approximate area.
The bars multiply into 50 thin slices, fitting the curve's shape much more precisely.
The slices blend into a semi-transparent orange (#FFA500) shaded area representing the total integral.
The label 'Accumulated Distance (Integral)' appears over the shaded region.

storyboard.title: The Grand Connection: Two Sides of the Same Coin
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
Derivatives break paths down into rates.
Integrals build those rates back into paths.
animations: A pink box (#FF69B4) labeled 'Differentiate' and a green box (#32CD32) labeled 'Integrate' appear side-by-side.
A mathematical expression 'f(x)' moves into the pink box and emerges as its derivative 'f'(x)'.
The 'f'(x)' then moves into the green box and returns as the original 'f(x) + C'.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Link: The Area Function
lecture_lines: Let's look at the original function curve.
We shade the area as we move right.
The top graph tracks total accumulated area.
Area growth rate matches the curve's height.
The derivative of area is the function.
animations: A function curve f(t) is drawn in lime green (#32CD32) on the bottom half of the screen.
A vertical line moves from left to right, shading the area under f(t) in light blue (#87CEEB).
An 'Area Function' graph A(x) is simultaneously drawn on the top half in orange-red (#FF4500).
A vertical dashed line connects the height of f(t) to the slope of A(x) to show their equality.
The formula 'A'(x) = f(x)' appears in a bold white font (#FFFFFF) to emphasize the link.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: The Universal Cycle
lecture_lines: Derivatives track speed; integrals track distance.
They form a perfect mathematical cycle.
Together, they unlock the secrets of change.
animations: A 'Speedometer' icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg] (#00FFFF) and an 'Odometer' icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/od.svg] (#FFD700) appear on the left and right.
Two white arrows (#FFFFFF) form a circular loop between the icons to illustrate the inverse cycle.
The words 'Derivative' and 'Integral' pulse in sync with the arrows to summarize the relationship.
